A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient polynomial time approximation scheme (PTAS) to solve the minimum routing cost spanning tree problem.

, given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ and a nonnegative cost on each edge $e \in E$, the routing cost of a spanning tree is the sum over the cost of the paths between all the pairs of vertices in the tree.

, for the problem of finding the minimum routing cost spanning tree in an undirected weighted graph, we have developed a polynomial-time approximation algorithm that achieves an approximation factor of 1 + $\varepsilon$. The running time of the algorithm is $O(n^{1/\varepsilon})$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the routing cost objective is a natural generalization of the shortest path objective, and that many techniques developed for the latter can also be applied to the former.
